plugins.name: mai-second-brain
plugins.description: Build and use your MAI Second Brain from your AI chat: map your projects, save chats as notes, get a daily web brief on your topics, and review your week.

skills.name: daily-brief
skills.description: Research the web on the topics the user follows, relate the news to their own work and projects, and save the result as a note in their MAI Second Brain, where they can read it later or tap Listen to hear it. Sets the topics up once, runs today's brief right away, and schedules it every morning where the app supports scheduled tasks. Use when the user says "daily brief", "morning brief", "brief me on my industry", "set up my daily brief" or "change my brief".

skills.name: map-my-brain
skills.description: Build the user's MAI Second Brain from what the assistant already knows about them. Recalls their projects, goals and ambitions from memory and past conversations, confirms them in a few quick questions, then creates projects, a brief note for each project, an "About me" note and their Current Focus in MAI. Use when the user says "map my brain", "set up my second brain", "fill my brain", "create my projects in MAI", or is new to MAI and has no projects yet.
headings: 3. Confirm in two or three short rounds
4. Show the plan and wait for a yes

skills.name: save-to-brain
skills.description: Save the current conversation to the user's MAI Second Brain as one clean, structured note filed in the right project, and turn its action items into tasks if the user wants. Use when the user says "save this to my brain", "save this chat", "add this to MAI", "put this in my notes", or wants to keep the outcome of a working session.

skills.name: weekly-review
skills.description: Run a weekly review of the user's MAI Second Brain covering what got done, what slipped, the week's themes and next week's focus, saved as a note. Then clear stale tasks with the user (done, reschedule or keep, one decision per task) and update their Current Focus, always with their say-so. Use when the user says "weekly review", "review my week", "Friday review", "what did I get done this week" or "plan next week".
